chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Jamhur, from his father, raising it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade the marriage of Shighaar, and it is Al-Mumanah, and it is that a man says to another man, 'Marry your daughter to me so that I may marry my daughter to you,' on the condition that there is no dower between them.
ai.seo_question: What is Shighaar marriage and why did the Prophet forbid it?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi defines 'Shighaar' as a pre-Islamic practice where two men exchange daughters in marriage without paying dowry (mahr) to either bride, a custom the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) explicitly forbade. In Shia jurisprudence, this prohibition underscores that mahr is an essential, distinct right of the wife, not merely a reciprocal barter, thereby preserving the dignity and financial security of women within the marital contract.
